input.description: The full recipe requires: KG/CG construction from source text with triple-to-chunk traceability, structured QA item generation for 1-5 hop reasoning, SFT of a ~14B model, multiple rounds of LLM-judged adaptive repair (each round requiring judge calls plus continual fine-tuning), a lower-hop RL stage, and evaluation on 3-5-hop items. This is a multi-stage, compute-heavy pipeline. It is unclear whether code/data from the closest work (arxiv:2609.12230) is released and whether the pipeline is reproducible within the investigation's compute budget, which determines whether any experiment plan can actually be executed.
input.question: Can the full context-augmented + repair + RL pipeline be reproduced or re-implemented feasibly (available code/data, judge and fine-tuning compute budget) for a ~14B LLM?
input.rationale: Feasibility gates whether an experiment plan is actionable at all; a search for the closest work's released code and for lower-cost substitutes (smaller backbone, public KGs) would change the plan's shape. No code link is recorded yet for arxiv:2609.12230.

input.description: The idea may exist under terminology absent from the initial queries. Related lines include context-aware/neighbor-aware knowledge graph completion (e.g., arxiv:2410.16803), GraphRAG and KG-RAG subgraph retrieval, subgraph-retrieval KBQA, and path-based RL reasoning. These could contain a context-attached-to-triple supervision mechanism framed differently, so the overlap boundary of the idea is not yet established and the contribution may be narrower or wider than the single closest paper suggests.
input.question: Does the context-augmented triple supervision mechanism already exist under alternative terminology (context-aware KGC, GraphRAG, subgraph retrieval, neighbor-aware embedding) that the initial searches did not cover?
input.rationale: Alternative terminology typically surfaces a different, partly overlapping literature; whether any of it supervises an LLM with a context subgraph attached to each target triple determines the real overlap boundary rather than a single-paper judgment.

input.description: The closest work reports that repair 'enables the models to reach 100% accuracy on the cleaned retained one-hop validation sets' and that it 'removes or quarantines problematic noisy triples' while updating the validation set with regenerated questions. Because the evaluation set is modified by the same loop that is being evaluated, observed one-hop and downstream gains may partly reflect evaluation-set cleaning/selection rather than genuinely repaired knowledge. An untouched, held-out one-hop and multi-hop test set that the repair loop never edits is needed to separate these.
input.question: Do the repair-loop gains reflect genuine knowledge repair, or are they inflated by cleaning/selecting the validation set that the loop itself operates on?
input.rationale: If gains are selection artifacts, hypothesis H2 and the motivation for the repair stage are substantially weakened; resolving this requires reading how the retained and refreshed validation sets were constructed (Section 3.6/3.8) and how quarantine interacts with evaluation.

input.description: The closest retrieved work evaluates with structured multiple-choice clinical QA items over two disease-specific KGs (Gastroparesis, Diabetes) and reports robustness to option shuffling. It is unclear whether the same mechanism would show gains under the standard multi-hop KGQA evaluation regime (WebQSP, ComplexWebQuestions, MetaQA) with answer exact-match/F1, or whether multiple-choice format and domain-specific item generation interact with the effect. Metric choice and benchmark choice therefore affect whether any measured improvement generalizes.
input.question: Which evaluation methodology (standard benchmarks with EM/F1 vs generated domain-specific multiple-choice items, and which metrics) is appropriate and would the effect replicate under it?
input.rationale: The evaluation setting determines comparability with the prior literature and whether a re-scoped contribution is measurable; standard-benchmark evidence has not been gathered, and metric-format confounds (multiple choice, option shuffling, judge-based scoring) are plausible.

input.description: Given that arxiv:2609.12230 appears to report the combined recipe and its comparative claim, continuing the original idea unchanged would likely be a replication. The defensible re-scoped questions (component-wise decomposition with matched-token controls; generalization beyond disease-specific KGs; distinguishing repair's real effect from validation-set cleaning; whether lower-hop RL transfers with seed-level significance) have not been ranked, and the decision of what to pursue is still open.
input.question: What re-scoped research question yields a defensible contribution after the closest work, and which of the candidate re-scopings is most valuable and most feasible?
input.rationale: Direction choice shapes every downstream step (which papers to compare, which experiment to plan); without ranking the re-scopings, the investigation risks planning experiments that merely reproduce known results. This uncertainty should be resolved after the overlap and confounding questions are investigated.

Recorded the investigation plan: 7 questions (closest methods, alternative terminology, baselines/evaluation methodology, feasibility, residual novel contribution, the context-vs-token-volume confounder, and RL-vs-SFT transfer), 14 search topics with alternative terminology (GraphRAG, context-aware KGC, RLVR/GRPO, STAT-style repair), and 11 comparison targets spanning subgraph-retrieval KBQA, KG-embedding KGQA, path-based RL, and LLM fine-tuned KGQA.

I also recorded five new uncertainties: U004 feasibility of reproducing the full pipeline, U005 overlap under alternative terminology, U006 whether repair gains are validation-set-cleaning artifacts, U007 benchmark/metric validity of domain-specific multiple-choice versus standard WebQSP/CWQ/MetaQA evaluation, and U008 the direction question of which re-scoped contribution remains defensible after arxiv:2609.12230.
